title: 20 January 1970: John Lennon and Yoko Ono have their hair cropped in Denmark
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono stayed in Aalborg in Denmark over the new year and most of January 1970, to be with Ono’s daughter Kyoko. She was living there with Tony Cox, Ono’s second husband, and his new wife Melinda.

While staying in Denmark Lennon made the decision to have his hair cropped shorter than at any other time in his adult life. The precise reasons are unclear, although he and Ono were in the midst of a lengthy peace campaign and were keen to remain in the public eye.

Lennon and Ono both had their hair cut on 13 January 1970. It was later described by the Daily Mirror as “the most sensational scalpings since the Red Indians went out of business”. The couple kept their shorn locks in a bag for future use.

The haircuts were done by Aase Haugkrogh, the resident stylist at the Hotel Hvide Hus in Aalborg. She was requested to attend by Cox, and was first asked to cut Kyoko’s hair.

Lennon then handed her his 1967 passport picture, asking that she cut his hair in a similar style. Afterwards she asked Ono if she would like the same done, but she declined, upset that Lennon’s hair had been removed. However, when asked a second time, Ono changed her mind and also had hers cut off.

After agreeing to keep the event secret, Haugkrogh was paid 200 kroner for her work, around ten times her usual rate. She also received a copy of Live Peace In Toronto 1969, the enclosed calendar of which Lennon signed with the words: “To Aasi with love and thanks for the HAIRCUTS From the SKINHEADS.”

On 4 February 1970 Lennon and Ono swapped the hair for a pair of Muhammad Ali’s bloodstained boxing shorts, which they said they intended to auction to raise money for peace.
